subject: science
chapter_title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

concepts.title: Why We Separate Substances
concepts.definition: Grain from the field arrives mixed with stones, husk and dust; separating useful from useless, or one useful part from another, keeps food clean and gives each component its own use.
concepts.key_idea: Separation is choosing: methods are picked to match the difference between the mixed things.

what impurities are found in harvested grain

concepts.title: Handpicking, Threshing and Winnowing
concepts.definition: Big unwanted bits are picked out by hand; grain is knocked out of stalks by threshing; and winnowing lets the wind blow the light husk away from the heavier grain falling from a height.
concepts.key_idea: Each method rides on a difference: size for handpicking, weight for winnowing, force for threshing.

concepts.title: Sieving and Settling Methods
concepts.definition: A sieve lets fine flour pass and holds back coarse bits; in water, heavy sand settles below lighter water in sedimentation and the clear top layer is poured off, while straining tea uses a mesh like a sieve.
concepts.key_idea: Sieves sort by particle size, settling sorts by weight: two more differences put to work.

concepts.title: Evaporation: Recovering Salt from Solution
concepts.definition: Salt dissolved in water cannot be picked or sieved out; heating the solution in a china dish evaporates the water and leaves salt crystals behind, the method used to make salt from seawater.
concepts.formula: salt_solution + heat = salt crystals + water vapour
concepts.key_idea: Evaporation reaches where sieves cannot: the dissolved substance stays back when the liquid flies away.
